subject: OrbitAI: three-region dedicated capacity ask (US / EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orbit.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-01 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for global feature launch

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising. We are planning a staged global launch of OrbitAI Search in Q4 and need dedicated capacity commitments to guarantee SLOs across three markets. High level ask below:

- US (primary): sustained 120 concurrent A100-class slots during business hours (peak 200k tokens/min).
- EU (Frankfurt): 60 A100-class sustained, 100k tokens/min peak.
- APAC (Singapore): initial 40 H100-class sustained, ramp to 80 in 6 weeks (model variant optimized for token efficiency).

Key constraints: data residency for EU, private peering in APAC, and we require a signed SOW + capacity commitment by 2025-09-10 to meet our launch timeline.

Can you confirm feasibility and an initial SOW draft? I attached our expected traffic curve (small CSV) — open to an initial tranche approach if needed.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships
OrbitAI
(attachment: orbit_traffic_curve_q4.csv, type: csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orbit.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-01 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for global feature launch

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic CSV. Quick read: feasible but needs trancheed procurement + a couple infra clarifications. Proposed next steps:

1) Internal sizing run (Irene) to map A100 vs H100 SKU mix and quantify cache/burst headroom.
2) Commercial tranches (Vanessa) — propose 30/40/30% commit split across months to accelerate provision.
3) Draft SOW and peering addendum (I will circulate a draft today).

Notes on constraints we saw up front: EU data residency requires Frankfurt-only hosts (no multi-region fallback unless encrypted KV cache policy accepted). APAC H100 provisioning could require 3-week lead for bare-metal nodes depending on date.

Laura — can you confirm product-side tolerance for model-variant fallbacks in EU?

Irene / Vanessa — can you run a quick capacity model and estimate timeline/cost delta for an A100-heavy vs H100-heavy approach? I attached a lightweight template for capacity modelling.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales — Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
(attachment: capacity_model_template.csv, type: csv)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for global feature launch

Rishi — starting the sizing run. Quick clarifying questions to make numbers realistic:

- Which model family are they serving in production (decoder-only vs. chat / multi-turn)? Tokenization & KV cache size changes sizing significantly.
- Are they expecting heavy streaming responses (latency-sensitive) or batch-like completion?
- For APAC you asked H100s — do they have a strict requirement for H100 or is an A100-optimized quantized build acceptable? H100s change preemption and procurement timelines.

If they can accept a mixed approach (A100 in US/EU, H100 in APAC for immediate low-latency), we can size a solution that pins hottest traffic to H100 while running most inference on A100 with aggressive KV cache. I will run three scenarios (A100-heavy, H100-heavy, hybrid) and push numbers by EOD.

Irene Choi
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orbit.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for global feature launch

Maria / team — attaching our initial capacity model for the tranche proposal. Summary of commercial and timing implications below:

Attachment: capacity_model_q3.csv (generated from Irene's sizing run)

Summary (high level):
- Option A (A100-dominant): US 120 A100-equivalent sustained; EU 60 A100; APAC 40 A100-as-H100-stand-in initially. Procurement lead: 2 weeks for node reservation + 3 weeks setup. Estimated incremental monthly run-rate: $XXXk.
- Option B (H100 in APAC): US 100 A100 + 20 H100 equivalent capacity (same latency SLO); EU unchanged. Procurement lead: 4+ weeks for H100s; monthly run-rate delta +22% (H100 premium).
- Tranche recommendation: 40% commit at signing (US priority), 30% in month 2, 30% in month 6 — this balances launch needs while allowing us to stagger physical node allocation.

We can shorten provision by using burst lanes (hosted shared fallback) for first 3 weeks — cost higher but guarantees GA. If Orbit wants strict dedicated-only from day 1, we need SOW signed and PO by 2025-09-05 to meet 2025-10-01 GA.

Next steps: 1) Maria — confirm preferred option (A or B) and tranche comfort, 2) Rishi/Laura — I will produce a short cost appendix for each option, 3) I will attach the SOW_draft_orbit_v2.pdf after we lock option.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Commercials
Redwood Inference
(attachment: capacity_model_q3.csv, type: csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orbit.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for global feature launch

Maria — appreciate the quick review. Based on internal input we recommend Option A with an APAC hybrid (A100 initially with H100 tag for rapid low-latency lanes) and the 40/30/30 tranche. That lets us guarantee US capacity day-one while we stage H100s if Orbit later elects to pay the delta.

Action items and timeline:
- Maria / Orbit procurement: confirm Option A and tranche acceptance by 2025-09-05 and provide PO.
- Vanessa: finalize cost appendix and SOW_draft_orbit_v2.pdf (target 2025-09-04 EOD).
- Irene: lock node allocation windows and provide final lead-time table — include burst-hosting fallback window and any data-residency caveats.
- Laura: notify product / infra about the EU-only residency requirement; we will include the peering appendix.

If Orbit can sign by 09/05 we will commit to the 10/01 customer GA target assuming no unexpected procurement delays.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales — Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
